name: Judgment, hell & the resurrection
about: The judgment seat, the end of the wicked, and today as the day of salvation.

teachings.title: Vengeance is His: the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The disobedient will meet Christ's coming in fear and everlasting destruction, and believers suffering tribulation can take heart that vengeance belongs to God and He is faithful.
teachings.text:
As for those who are disobedient to the Gospel, this day is met with fear.

**Revelation 6:15-17**
*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

Or as Paul writes in **2 Thessalonians 2:9** they *shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.*

The martyrs in Heaven, especially those killed in the Great Tribulation, cry out for vengeance and the firey judgment of God. God's promise is that they will receive fire and damnation for their wickedness, and all shall know His power.

God is longsuffering, and His timing may frustrate us as man, as He does not count the time as we do, "a thousand years as a day," the way Peter describes, but His promise is true, and He is faithful to those of us who have faith in His Son.

Vengeance is His. Take heart in that, though the world may hate us, though we may know tribulation, we, like the Thessalonicans can take heart.

**Matthew 16:27** *For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.*

teachings.title: Heaven is real and Hell is eternal torment
teachings.summary: Matthew 25 and Revelation show a real Kingdom of Heaven and a Hell of eternal fiery torment in the presence of the Lamb, against those who call it unjust or mere separation.
teachings.text:
Finally, there is a wicked doctrine that circulates among the unsaved, pushed by vipers that there is no Kingdom of Heaven, that our reward and inheritance is of the earth, and that there is no Hell, that the damned do not face eternal torment and burning for their sin. Many pushing this false doctrine claim Jesus never spoke of either, and that Hell and the grave are the same.

Some use corrupt versions of the Bible to claim foolish things such as Sheol being different than Hades, that "Abraham's bosom" is a place rather than a body part, a paradise inside or along side Hell. They use semantics and concordances, pedantic reasoning and ignore the actual text and context regarding both. It has been a snare and a stumbling block for many.

Some see the idea of eternal punishment as 'unjust,' and like the unprofitable servant, accuse God of being unjustified in His condemnation. Others will paint believers as the offenders, offering up an "unfair" God, when, in their mind, God is love and so he "wouldn't subject people to eternal torment just for not believing in Jesus."

They may even trot out the old "what about the savage in the jungle, hmm? Is *that* fair??" chestnut.

All of this is natural man foolishness as both the promise of Heaven and eternal life, along with Hell and eternal torment are given throughout scripture, and as just **Matthew 25** demonstrates.

Jesus says the Kingdom of Heaven is like the wedding of the bridegroom, to which the 5 wise virgins are let in to, the door shut to the fools, whom the bridegroom says he never knew. He doesn't say the millennial reign on earth. He doesn't say the New Earth of revelation. He consistently says the Kingdom is of Heaven. It is our promise and reward, both now after our physical death, (*to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord*) and our inheritance in the resurrection.

But what of Hell? Is it simply being shut out of Heaven? Again, in **Matthew 25** Jesus tells us details of the unbelievers' fate.

Of the unprofitable servant, He says "*cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth."* This is a formula used throughout Matthew by Jesus to describe Hell. Wailing and gnashing of teeth. Torment and agony. But is 'outer darkness' Hell?

**Revelation 14** says of the damned; *The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

Tormented with fire and brimstone, the smoke of their torment ascending forever and ever. Sounds like Hell.

As an aside, some wishy-washy Christians will claim that Hell is actually just the "separation from Jesus," when here we see the burning torment of the damned is done *in* His presence.

**Revelation 20** tells us;
*the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever...And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

Further, **Revelation 21**; *But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.*

And **Revelation 22**, after telling of those who have overcome are within the Holy City, that *without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.*

teachings.title: Everlasting fire, everlasting punishment
teachings.summary: Jesus said the wicked go into everlasting fire and punishment, so Hell is a real place, now in the pit of the earth and later the lake of fire.
teachings.text:
Back in **Matthew 25**, Jesus says "*Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels....And these shall go away into everlasting punishment.*"

Everlasting fire. Everlasting punishment. But to the righteous, life eternal.

This is the biblical teaching on Hell. It's a real place, in the pit of the earth for now, and later cast into the outer darkness, the lake of fire, after the physical world is destroyed, after the millennium has ended and the White Throne Judgment of the unrighteous is done.

So do not be fooled. Hell is very real, and God is not slack regarding His promises. He is perfectly righteous and holy. And if He says throughout His word that eternal torment, punishment, burning, is what awaits those not clothed in the righteousness of Jesus then you can believe it is true.

teachings.title: The last shall be first, and hell fire for offenders
teachings.summary: Greatness in the kingdom comes from serving the least, those who offend little ones face a hotter hell, and denying hell is a damnable heresy that removes the need for salvation.
teachings.text:
We come to Jesus's teaching in Capernaum to the Apostles.

He asked them what they had been swabbling about between themselves and they reply embarrassed, over which of them shall be first among them. A very human thing, stemming from pride.

And Jesus famously answers, but the first shall be last and the last shall be first. Many misunderstand this, and create confusing feel-good doctrines, but as Mark chapter 9 gives us the full teaching, we can understand that it is in service to the least that we become the first. It's serving those in Jesus name who are weaker, children, the poor, the widow. Pure religion undefiled. It is in that service that willingness to be last, to be least, to be humble servants, that elevates our status in the Kingdom of Heaven. That gives honor and Glory to God.

Jesus uses a helpless innocent, a child, as a picture of what this means. That the things we do for the least among Us elevate us.  To  do without for others, meekly abasing ourselves for others benefit.

And using the same child, Jesus transitions to those that rather than serving, offend. Offense in the Bible in this context, refers to obstacles to faith, things taking you away from the word. Stumbling blocks.

And of those who rather than serve the week, the innocent, the children rather seek to offend them, that is hurt them in a way that brings them from the faith, Jesus says it is better that they kill themselves. That they would be better off tying a millstone around their neck and throwing themselves into the ocean then to bring a fence, to place a stumbling block, to traumatize a child with their own wickedness. Groomers and pedophiles, sodomites and the wicked of this world are better off killing themselves early then racking up offenses, in its other meaning. Because the fires of hell that awaits them will burn hotter for them for this.

Just as the last shall be first, elevated in the kingdom of heaven and rewarded for their service to the least among Us, so too will the punishment of eternal Hell be that much worse for those who offend the same.

There is a foolish false Doctrine out there that says there is no such thing as a fiery hell awaiting those who have died in sin, without coming to Faith in God the Father and His Son.

Rather than use the Bible they use concordances and the writings of men in an attempt to deny the concept of perdition in a lake of fire or in the Hell below us.

These unsaved fools, perishing, deny the very existence of the thing that we need salvation from to teach a false gospel that it is just "the grave."

These fools who deny the perfect justice of God to teach damnable heresy with pride and arrogance, are literally an offense, a stumbling block to those who are seeking the truth.

For if there is no hell then there is no punishment for our transgressions that we need to be saved from. If there is only oblivion and the grave, there's nothing to escape.

*Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?*

How indeed.

Like the sadducees, they deny the promise of Heaven, as well as the reality of Hell, and like them, are vipers, leading others astray.

For if there's not a Hell, what do we need salvation for. And if there is no Heaven, what then is the eternal reward? Eat drink and be merry for tomorrow you die.

But we as saved Christians look forward to a better country, a Heavenly Kingdom.

InB4 "the Kingdom of Heaven is on Earth" Sperg response.

That's like saying the kingdom of England isn't in England. The kingdom of France is in China.

It's pure foolishness of a natural man seeking to lean into his own understanding and private interpretation. And it's wicked as the Hell they deny.

And like most false doctrine, we only have to read scripture to see what God says. And here, Jesus gives us an understanding of the nature of Hell, while giving us an understanding of sin of the flesh which damns us to it.

teachings.title: The fire that never shall be quenched
teachings.summary: In Mark 9 Jesus Himself describes hell as literal unquenchable fire in God's presence, not mere annihilation or the grave, which is why sinners need saving.
teachings.text:
Since we are condemned under the law, and sin is transgression of the law, Jesus says it is better to physically cut off a limb or pluck out our eye than enter into Hell. And lucky for us, we have liberty from that fate, through faith in Christ and His imputed righteousness, so that we aren't hobbling around half blind to avoid damnation.

But note what Jesus tells us about Hell. Christ describes Hell as a place of *fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.*

He says sinners will be *cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched,* *cast into hell fire.*

This isn't allegory. It's not a parable. It isn't a mistranslation of the Greek, or a later doctrine cobbled together by extra-Biblical sources.

It is how Jesus Christ, the word made flesh, describes the eternal damnation of Hell. Also, outer darkness, where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth. Where the smoke of their torment rises forever. Burned of the fire that comes forth from God, and the damned are burned in Christ's presence, along with Satan and the fallen, for eternity.

We don't even need to do a full study of Hell in the Bible to arrive at this point, we can simply take Jesus' word for it here in Mark 9.

It is not just the grave. It isn't being outside the presence of God, in fact the Bible says it is in His presence this torment occurs. It isn't a place ruled by the Devil, he burns alongside those he deceived.

If you do not believe that we have a reward, a wage, due us by our sin, and applied by a just and loving God for those who loved the world more than Him, then you have no reason to believe you need saving. Repent and believe that you may be spared this fate.

teachings.title: Hell Is Real, Eternal Torment
teachings.summary: Hell is a real place of eternal torment in the presence of the Lamb, not the grave, annihilation or Satan's kingdom, so some must be saved with fear.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 14**
*8 And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.*

*9 And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand,*

*10 The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb:*

*11 And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

Continuing chapter 14, we see angels proclaiming first the Gospel, then in verse 8, hailing the destruction of Babylon. This will be dealt with in somewhat greater detail in chapter 17.

The third angel heralds the damnation of those who worship the beast and take his mark, their place in wrath and Hell assured. And important doctrine is found in these verses; that Hell is real, eternal, and that the torment of the damned takes place in the presence of the Lamb, Christ Jesus.

There are false doctrines that make many claims regarding Hell, or what happens in death to those unregenerate souls who don't accept the free gift of salvation. Satan and his children have tried to cast doubt on Hells existence, claiming it is simply the grave, "Sheol." Barring that, they will say it's not eternal, that the soul is consumed and annihilation is swift.

Others claim that Hell is just a dark empty void, or being cut off from the presence of God, which they claim is worse than simply being tormented by fire.

And of course there are those who claim Satan himself is ruler of Hell and his demons are tormenting spirits used against the damned, pitchforks and devils.

But the Bible tells us these are heretical and silly views, and none more clearly than here in Revelation.

The souls are condemned to be bound in Hell with the Devil. Hell was created especially for Satan and his fallen angels, according to Jesus in **Matthew 25:41** "*Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.*"

God's wrath is a fire that pours out from Him, and the damned are tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels and Christ, the smoke of their torment rises up for eternity, and they have no rest day or night from this torment.

This is why we are called to be servants of the Lord who saved us. To be a light unto the world and give testimony to the Gospel. Saving some with kindness and charity, magnifying the grace God has extended on we who are saved, that it may guide those seeking the light to the truth. But some require more than that. They require fear. Fear of judgment and the punishment, the wages of their sin. The Bible says those we should *save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

teachings.title: The White Throne Judgment of the Dead
teachings.summary: The great white throne judges the damned blotted out of the book of life, who go to the lake of fire, and only faith in Christ escapes that judgment.
teachings.text:
Here we are given the Millennial Reign in fewer than 15 verses. The binding of Satan in Hell. The saints ruling and reigning the earth in judgment with Christ for that period. Those that sacrificed the most for the cause of Christ given more authority. Until the little season where Satan is given freedom to convince the living humans on earth who resent the rule to rise up against Jesus and the saints. They are destroyed in a moment by fire. Death and then the judgment.

The Great White Throne judgment is of the dead. The damned. Great and small, whose names were blotted out of the Book of Life. Judged by the books of the law, the scriptures of God. His precepts. Written in our hearts, His wrath written in all of creation, that man may have no excuse. And they all have the second death, the lake of fire, the final place of Hell and death, to be tormented for eternity.

Remember, no where in scripture does it say any of one gets written into the Book of Life. It was written before creation, and contains every one that lives. Who are then blotted out if they be reprobate or die without the testimony of Jesus. We can only escape the judgment by faith. Accepting the free gift of salvation given by grace from God.

**Matthew 7**
*21 Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.*

*22 Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?*

*23 And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.*

**John 6:40**
*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**Ephesians 2:8-9**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.*

**Titus 2**:**12-13**
*For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: Heaven and Hell are real: the rich man and Lazarus
teachings.summary: Jesus' parables are built on real things, so the rich man and Lazarus shows Heaven and Hell are real, while Abraham's bosom as a waiting compartment is a dispensationalist error.
teachings.text:
I would be remiss if I didn't address some of the contentions that come from this parable.

There are some who take this teaching of Jesus and draw conclusions from it for doctrine that amount to them attempting to fit their square pegs into round holes. Who are applying the logic of men to the things of God.

There are some who deny Heaven and Hell entirely and to them they will say that this parable shouldn't be used to justify the doctrines of Heaven and Hell being real, fixed places in the cosmos. And the destination of the dead be they saved or unsaved.

They take a general rule of thumb that is true and apply it here in a way that's foolish. We shouldn't draw doctrine from parables taken literally. We aren't literally having the faith of a mustard seed. We aren't literally sowing seeds upon the ground. We aren't literally sheep, the enemy's not literally wolves. We are supposed to see that creation serves as a way of understanding God's word, which is spirit and which is life.

But what they fail to understand is that every parable that Jesus tells is of something we can understand. Of something real. Of lamps and oil and weddings and servants, of lords and stewards. Sowing seeds and harvesting the fruit. Jesus consistently uses creation as the backbone of his parables so that man can relate to what he's saying and take from it. The spiritual application that He's providing. That's no different here. God is not the author of confusion, and Jesus doesn't make things up.

So even if this is simply a parable and not an actual retelling of events, it still uses as its basis, reality. Identifyable and understandable concepts. Death and the life thereafter, or condemnation to Hell which is burning and fire.

Another mistaken doctrine that stems from this is the idea that Abraham's bosom is a place and not a body part. That prior to Jesus crucifixion there was no Heaven and Hell but waiting areas, that Lazarus went to a paradise that is part of Hell. That Jews who were saved in the Old Testament, All of the Israelite saints, that when they die they went to Abraham's bosom rather than to Heaven where Abraham awaited.

This is often paired with dispensationalist heresies. It's foolishness and the other extreme of using parables for doctrine.

We can't say for certain that the Lazarus of this story is Jesus's friend from Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha whom Jesus loved. But it's unusual for Jesus in a parable to use the specific name rather than a certain descriptor. It's not that important that we know this detail for sure. It's the spiritual application of the parable that matters. That there are some who see the richness of life as sumptuous living and worldly success. Who serve mammon rather than God. And their ability to believe, to come to saving faith is hampered by their pride and arrogance. Their hypocrisy and covetousness. They're placing the justification before men above being justified by God.

There is a Heaven and there is a Hell and there is more to this life than the things that we store up here on earth.

Don't allow your comfort or your wealth or your respect among your peers to confuse you regarding salvation. All have fallen short and failed to uphold God's law. And don't allow the low status of some to make you see them as less than. Don't be a respecter of persons.

teachings.title: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever
teachings.summary: The boastful wicked who reject the fear of the Lord face eternal torment in hell, and believers should name them plainly and preach that hard truth so some may be pulled out of the fire.
teachings.text:
In **Psalm 52**, the psalmist presents the polar opposite of the contrite heart of **Psalm 51**, the mischief-making man who doesn't avail himself to the longsuffering mercy of God.

The wicked and their deceitful tongue, inventing lies, telling slander against God and God's people, boasting of their blessings, not thankful but vain in their imagination, loving evil more than good, these are the men who continually reject the call to fear the Lord.

Those of us who are saved can become incredulous at the prideful stance of the wicked, who reject the fear of God and lean on their own strength. We can often grow confounded and even depressed over the ways of the wicked. Like just Lot, living in Sodom, being afflicted by the wickedness around him

**2 Peter 2:8**
(*For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

The Bible is not afraid to call these people out, directly and to their face. They are boastful, mockingly called "mighty men," liars, evil, haters of righteousness, lovers of slanderous and wicked words, lovers of mischief, having deceitful tongues.

We should not fear to identify exactly the perverted in our midst when they reject and mock the gospel of God and the word we preach.

Nor should we tiptoe around the heart of the matter; Their immanent destruction and the torment in the fire of Hell that awaits them.

**Jude 1:22–23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

Those who do not see the wrath of God revealed from Heaven upon others as a reason to repent and believe, and won't see the mercy and hear the praise of the meek, feeling the compassionate love of believers magnify God's grace, need hard preaching to let them know exactly what they've chosen, in hopes that they might be saved.

That their love of devouring words will lead to God likewise destroying them forever. Literally, being devoured by flame and worm in outer darkness, forever. Eternal suffering at the hands of a just and mighty God.

*God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living.* *Selah*.

If "selah" is meant to be a pause, a moment to reflect on what was just sung or said, is there anywhere more fitting than in that moment, having heard that sobering truth?

God will destroy you. He will take your life and root you out of the land of the living, to place you in a place of eternal destruction.

And the righteous shall see their end and fear God, and laugh at the calamity they brought about on themselves. The end their mischief brought about, turned back upon them.

**Proverbs 26:27**
*Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him*.

The ironic nature of the bitter end experienced by the boastful sinner is often evident and clear to those that fear God. The humor of the Lord is appreciated by His children. We laugh at their calamity.

When the wicked are made a parable or a byword among the people, it should give other men pause. The wrath revealed from Heaven should give instruction to the simple to turn towards God. It shows the righteous in Christ God's power and promise.

**Proverbs 1:7**
*The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

The warning is ignored by the fool. And God will not be mocked.

**Proverbs 1:25–30**
*But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.*

teachings.title: Gold and silver, or wood, hay and stubble
teachings.summary: On the one foundation of Christ our works will be tried by fire, and only what glorifies God such as soul winning and charity is rewarded while worldly disputes, denominations and traditions burn as stubble.
teachings.text:
Remember, this letter to the church at Corinth is to rebuke strife and divisions regarding earthly things among spiritual brethren. Paul uses carnal, of the flesh, to refer to the things of this world that aren't spiritual. He says he can't even speak to them of spiritual things because they are yet carnal. Babes in Christ who barely can digest the milk of the word, let alone the meat, the harder things of God. His reproach is to say they are yet carnal, and he gives evidence of their arguments over who they got saved by. What minister of God planted the seed or watered that seed or harvested them unto repentance towards God is unimportant. All believers have a minister from who they heard the word, and believing the word, had faith. We are all called to be such ministers, but to God is the increase. To God is the bounty that none of the husbandmen can glory.

And when we are in heaven, our works in this regard will be judged. And what we do will be determined by fire, as to whether or not it is wood hay and stubble, to be burned away as unimportant, or precious jewels and gold and silver with which we will be rewarded for our labor.

Things of hay and stubble will be these unimportant worldly matters in which we might be right, or diligent in what we do, but with no real spiritual value. Nothing that adds to the glory of God or magnifies His word.

Winning souls to Christ, helping the poor and the fatherless, the widows, being doers of the word and not hearers only, those things are rewarded by God in the judgment.

Our common foundation is Jesus Christ, and what we build upon that foundation honestly comes down to whether it gives glory to God or not. And your going to the right denomination, adhering to traditions of men, engaging in sacraments and rites, having the correct opinion about a political dispute or a question of genealogies, or the shape of the realm that we inhabit... All of that is wood, hay and stubble.

Don't get it confused, and be carnal. Seek the higher things of God comparing spiritual with spiritual, and in your discipleship put away the strife and divisions that the world serves up to us. They are snares. And they use our own pride and subjective nature as hooks to snare us on.

This is what Paul means by being a fool to the world. We should know nothing other than what God reveals, because the wisdom of the world is foolishness to Him.

teachings.title: The talents: same joy, different rule
teachings.summary: The faithful servants both enter the joy of the Lord though given different rule, while the unprofitable servant represents the unsaved who thought wickedly of God and refused His gift.
teachings.text:
The next is the parable of the good and faithful servants, and the unprofitable one. In this familiar story, Jesus tells us of a wealth man, gone on a journey, leaving to each of his servants his goods to watch over. Divided according to their ability. Given talents according to their talent.

The one who received 5 talents doubled it, and he who received 2 did the same. But the one to whom the lord offered one, took it and buried it and had no use of it at all.

When the master returns, after a long time Jesus emphasizes, each gives an account. The 2 servants who have used what was given unto them to increase the master's wealth, and are rewarded for their efforts.

To each, he says "*Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord."*

Note that to both is given the same reward, though what each is made ruler over may differ. Jesus uses the same wording for both in this teaching of the Kingdom of Heaven for a reason. While we may be given responsibility based on our talents, our salvation, entering I to the joy of the Lord is the same. And so, while one may do great things for the Lord and be given greater responsibility in the Kingdom, and another given less, but just as faithful, is given less responsibility, both are entered into the Kingdom. Both are given to the joy of the Lord having accepted the responsibility while He was away.

And to the unprofitable servant, who didn't take the responsibility, but despised it. Who the lord expected little of. He just buried it until the return, not even joining in where the work of others may have given increase to what he was left. He is an unsaved person who knowing of Jesus, thought wickedly of Him, and didn't accept the gift of salvation, not even to just be partaker of the joy of the Lord.

The unprofitable servant gives his excuse; "*Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed*."

It is important to remember that in scripture, what a man might say, especially one representative of the unsaved, isn't necessarily true. That while the narration of the Bible is truth, the words uttered by characters aren't always. Jesus is not a cruel master. We see this in the parable where he takes into account our ability, and asks little of us considering. He rewards generously those good and faithful to Him.

So the unprofitable servant claims it was fear of an unjust Lord that led him to squander and reject that which was given him.

And the Lord says if that were true, and you actually thought that of me, you'd have at least tried out of fear.

Many who refuse to believe claiming the worst of God, that He is unjust, and takes what isn't His to take, don't actually follow through on their fear. For if they believed it, they'd have done their duty out of that fear.

God prefers we accept the gift, the salvation He offers and to make the most of what's given us, out of love and loyalty to Him. But He isn't opposed to it being received in fear for His wrath.

teachings.title: Souls won, our crown of rejoicing
teachings.summary: Every soul we help bring to Christ is our joy and crown at His coming, the gold that remains when our works are tried by fire.
teachings.text:
Wrapping up the chapter, Paul laments having spent little time with them, wishing it could have been more and, regretting that Satan had hindered his plans to return to them, assures that they will be together at Christ's return, and as souls won, be Paul and Silas' glory and joy. A crown of rejoicing, given as reward.

Every soul we help bring towards Christ and reconciliation with God through the blood of the lamb, whether it be a seed sown, watered or harvested, is our glory and joy in Christ's coming. Our reward at His judgment of our works. A crown given us, a precious stone, after the wood, hay and stubble are burned away.

**1 Corinthians 3:9-15**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*

*If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

teachings.title: A crown of righteousness for all who love His appearing
teachings.summary: Paul charges Timothy to preach the word in season and out, and finishes his course assured of the crown of righteousness that all who love Christ's appearing will receive when works are tried.
teachings.text:
I'm not crying you are crying.

Paul, having come close to the end of his life, having written to Timothy, his son in Christ whom he led to salvation, grew in the faith, laid hands on for the gifts of the Holy Ghost and sent out into Asia Minor to evangelize and spread the gospel, planting churches, charging his protege with teaching the fundamentallist doctrines of God, reaches his summation. A poignant and inspiring end.

Paul charges Timothy on God, in the name of Jesus, who will judge the quick and the dead, the living and the damned at His coming, to please be faithful to the doctrines he's left him.

*Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine.*

The word of God must be preached, we must be ready with scripture, when it's popular and when it isn't, especially. For we must be, as Timothy, ready to use all scripture to teach, strengthen and correct those seeking truth. To whom God has called to us in the Holy Spirit.

And this cause is great because, as Paul warns, people will wax cold to the truth, and turn towards fables and false doctrines that satisfy their itching ears, that justify and rationalize their sin, rather than lead them to the truth. So, as a stalwart in the faith, armed with the word, we, like Timothy must endure, for the sake of the elect that they may know the grace of God and His salvation.

And we understand Paul's plea, that he facing uncertainty, and his impending death in this life, seeks to ensure the tradition of the Gospel lives on in his "son."

*For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:*

*Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.*

This is the crown we should all strive for, the reward of those who work towards His coming.

The Bible says; *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth. and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven.*

For Jesus will judge the quick, as well as the dead. We who believe and are given the gift of eternal life will see our works judged;

*Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*  *If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

As Paul says, *Every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.*

And in Paul's striving for mastery, his running a good race, having fought the good fight, he knows with certainty as his end approaches, with that blessed assurance of the Spirit testifying within him, by the word that he has his hope in, that he will be rewarded by God as promised. For God is not slack regarding His promises. He is faithful in all things. Amen

teachings.title: We are the tabernacle
teachings.summary: In Christ we are the temple, and the works we build on Christ's foundation will be tried by fire, with gold, silver and precious stones rewarded.
teachings.text:
Paul was a tentmaker, like Bezaleel and Aholiab, who crafted the Tabernacle, the church in the wilderness wherein the children of Israel who sought the Lord would go to be in His presence. But in Christ, we are the Tabernacle, we are the temple. Our bodies the house of the Lord, made just as cunningly and with care. And we may build up our faith the way those whose heart the Lord put wisdom, and in their free will offerings the way our service to the Lord does.

**1 Corinthians 3:10-15**
*According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We bring our works to Christ at the resurrection, and the gold, silver and precious stones we give Him freely. Those saved or comforted by our good works. Those things with no value are burned away, and we are rewarded for what remains.

teachings.title: Jesus will judge every man by his works
teachings.summary: Christ will judge all by their works, the dead unto the lake of fire and the saved not for justification but for rewards in the kingdom.
teachings.text:
Jesus will judge every man for their works.

You heard me. The Lord Jesus Christ will judge every man according to his works.

*I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom.*

The dead, the unbelieving and disobedient.

**Revelation 20**
*11 And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.*

*12 And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.*

*13 And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.*

*14 And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.*

*15 And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

The quick being those alive in Christ. Saved by faith in Him alone. And when we are judged, it isn't for our justification, Jesus paid that price for us. God extended His grace to us that our sins and iniquities are forgotten.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

**Psalm 103:12**
*As far as the east is from the west, So far hath he removed our transgressions from us.*

**Romans 3**
*23 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;*

*24 Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:*

*25 Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;*

*26 To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

Amen.

But what about those works Jesus will judge, if it's not for justification, if it's not to be a propitiation for our sins so we don't have to pay the price of death and Hell, but have eternal life with Him, then why is He judging our works?

**1 Corinthians 3**
*9 For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building.*

*10 According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.*

*11 For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

*12 Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;*

*13 Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*

*14 If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.*

*15 If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

God rewards us for our works in the Kingdom of God. He pays His laborers. He judges us by how we do His will. By the charity, the love we show others. By the edification of His congregation. The building up of those saved by the good news that Jesus paid our debt to the law that we may be alive in grace.

Amen

teachings.title: The wages of sin and the gift of God
teachings.summary: Eternal life is a gift not a wage, and the saved, made servants of righteousness, earn rewards judged by fire at the judgment seat while never losing salvation.
teachings.text:
*Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.*

We are free to serve God being pardoned by His grace. To work for righteousness, as its servant out of love for Him that justified the ungodly, while we were yet sinners.

We who deserved death now are servants of life, unto God and should act like it. Note also in his appeal to walk in the new man, we are never told that we should lose the grace we standfast in. Rather, that we have our fruit unto holiness and the end everlasting life. We now earn rewards in the kingdom heaven, vs earning the wages of sin which is death.

*For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Gift vs wage. We do not earn gifts. A wage is debt owed. In sin, our debt is paid by death and hell, but in Christ we are given grace, a free gift, salvation and liberty that we may serve Him. And in that service we earn holiness, towards the righteousness of God, rewards.

**1 Corinthians 3:9-15**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We see here that as laborers for God, working as husbandmen in His vineyard, servants of His righteousness, that we will be judged as laborers, and earn rewards for our works. Each deed we do that is built up on the foundation of Christ will be judged by fire, and those of no spiritual importance will burn like wood, hay and stubble, but those of lasting impact, especially the salvation of souls, will be manifest as gold, silver and precious stones. And though some of our effort is burned by fire, as a loss, not being of real value, we ourselves are still saved, yet so as by fire. The same fire that reveals the fruit of our labors will be to us who believe a refining fire, but to them without hope, destruction in eternal torment.

*For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

God repays. Be it the wages of sin with death or rewards in the kingdom to come.

teachings.title: Faithful over a few things
teachings.summary: Freed from sin, we should live in love and service, because faithfulness with our talents now determines our rule in the Millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
Throughout the epistle to the Romans, we see Paul in the Spirit, building stone upon stone the doctrines of theology upon the foundation of Christ. The implications of our faith and the religion of following it.

That God gave His only begotten Son Christ Jesus, that by faith we are saved from the grip of death and the wrath of Hell. Every man. Jew and Gentile. Great and lowly. God is not a respecter of persons.

We are in the flesh, and sinful, even once we are saved, spirit quickened, and sealed by His Spirit, unto the day of redemption. But that being our hope, we know that in that day we will be raised, corruptible to incorruptible, into everlasting life.

And so, being freed from the burden of sin and death, we then should live like it. As much as possible live peaceably with all men. Loving our neighbors. Loving our enemies. Seeking the profit of our brethren. Serving our masters in our work as if we are working for God himself, because we are.

Showing mercy, as mercy has been shown us. Longsuffering as God has with us. Obedient, as Christ was obedient to the cross, even for our sakes. Even as we were enemies of God, that we may, in Him not only have peace with the Father, but become heirs to the Kingdom. Adopted brothers of Christ. That we may rule and reign with Him in the Millennial Kingdom. *Don't you know we shall judge angels?*

And if heirs to a kingdom, princes. And if princes, then we are servants ministering to those we have rule over.

And our ministry is determined by our willingness to sacrifice and serve here on Earth. We are given talents of silver by the master while He is gone. And some of us will seek its increase, and use the talents given us to bring forth more, that the Lord at His return can say *Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things*.

teachings.title: Deliver them that are drawn unto death
teachings.summary: Every man is judged by his works, believers at the bema seat for reward and the lost at the Great White Throne, so a believer who fails to give the gospel to the perishing cannot plead ignorance and will suffer loss.
teachings.text:
Continuing the fatherly advice of the King, Solomon, to his son the prince,  **Proverbs 24:11-12**;

*If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?*

He says that failure to deliver someone marked for death by claiming ignorance to the circumstances, and potentially the injustice or false accusations that led to it, by not hearing the matter fully - that it is not an excuse. Solomon writes that we should consider our own soul, the Lord's mercy upon it, His judgment. That He will judge every man according to his works.

This is echoed in the New Testament.

**Romans 2:4-9**
*Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile*

**Hebrews 9:27**
*And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.*

The wages of sin is death. We are all guilty. We will all be judged. But those in faith, who have believed on Christ, our sins not being imputed against our record, being justified by the righteousness of Jesus, our works, being built upon that foundation, are judged at the bema seat of Christ, to see what sort of works they are.

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We are still saved, but, based on the criteria of God; the good will be rewarded and the vain and meaningless, destroyed.

Meanwhile, the unbelieving are judged by their works at the Great White Throne. Their works held against them;

**Revelation 20:11-15**
*And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

With this perspective, which Solomon clearly understood, a ruler must make the effort to know what he is judging, especially in a capital crime where a life hangs in jeopardy.

This warning applies to those that are princes by faith, in the Kingdom of God. To believers, every man we meet is appointed to death and Hell for their sins. They are drawn unto death, and ready to be slain.

If we forbear to deliver them, to give them the gospel, we cannot say we didn't know. He that pondereth the heart and keepeth our soul, He knows it. And it will be counted a loss in the trying fire at the judgment seat of Christ.

teachings.title: To day if ye will hear his voice
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: God's call and light last only for a time, as the door of the ark was shut, so the unbelieving must repent and believe on Christ today.
teachings.text:
The meat of the word, giving us instruction on how we should carry ourselves as saved Christians, to be a good witness, to live faith to faith, growing in the spirit, studying to be approved unto God, understanding the liberty we have in Christ, what the implications are for those of us possessing eternal life, what to expect at Jesus' coming, God's plan and promise, His justice and wrath...all this is impossible to understand without first understanding salvation in Christ. Without which you cannot receive even the milk of the word, as born again babes.

The light of the Lord shines on us for a brief time, the Spirit convicts and draws the unbelieving to the light for a limited time, and then if a person remains unreceptive, is hid away. God gives every opportunity to you to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for salvation, but it isn't limitless.

*To day if ye will hear his voice,*
*Harden not your heart...behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation...Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near!*

Just as God was longsuffering to the unbelieving as Noah built his ark, and then shut the door, too late to be saved, so to is His offer of grace.

*While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

If you have not believed on Jesus Christ as the ONLY means of forgiveness and righteousness, if you have not accepted God's free gift of salvation, if you have been being called to the wedding feast, but have made excuse not to accept, or are trying to work your way in, repent.

Tomorrow is not promised. You are being called today. Don't wait until it is too late. Don't harden your heart.

teachings.title: Today If Ye Will Hear His Voice
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: As unbelief kept Israel out of the promised land, unbelief keeps men from God's rest, which is entered now by faith while the call lasts.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 again builds on the previous; **Hebrews 3**
*For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief*.

*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.*

Therefore, because, their unbelief in the desert prevented them from entering the promised land, so too fear your unbelief keeping you from entering into the promised land, the rest in Jesus, the better country; the Kingdom of Heaven.

By drawing the comparison to the Hebrews fleeing Egypt with those called coming out of bondage of the law and sin, Paul shows God's grace and His judgment parallels with Exodus spiritually. That it was a picture of Christ that so many Hebrews failed to believe and so died in the wilderness.

For we which have believed do enter into rest. Note the tense. Salvation comes by belief at the moment we call upon His name. At that time we are freed of bondage and given rest, and it is done by the work God finished from the foundation of the world.

**Genesis 2:2**
*And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.*

Paul argues that **if** God says (again quoting **Psalm 95**) *If they shall enter into my rest,* that we can reckon that this is a possible thing, offered by God, **and** those whom it was first preached didn't enter their promised land due to unbelief, **then** we can know we will enter into His rest by faith, and be kept out without it.

And further, as the Spirit moved Paul to write in **Psalm 95**; *Today if ye will hear His voice*, the offer is limited. We have but a short life to believe. A window of His calling, that can pass by death or prolonged neglect to hear His voice. To ignore it. To not retain God in their knowledge. Harden not your hearts when being called.

 *(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

God is reasoning with man, giving us the good news and His terms. Providing examples of what He means, and the if-then logic of it all that none have excuse. Harden not your hearts, hear His voice, NOW is the day of salvation. Believe or be shut out of the promise; never enter into His rest.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: Remember thy Creator before it is too late
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: Solomon's conclusion that all is vanity calls men to remember their Creator now, before death or the darkened sun of the day of the Lord, when it will be too late to fear Him.
teachings.text:
The end of Solomon's sermon, the preacher has spoken. Life is vanity and vexation of spirit, man toils and dies. There is iniquity and wickedness. Time and chance. A time for every purpose under Heaven. No guarantee of tomorrow. Only fleeting moments of joy where God has blessed us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. We should rejoice in our youth and remember the darkness, reflecting in mourning more than reveling in mirth. We should seek wisdom and reject foolishness, and in all things remember that there is a God, and He is just in His judgment.

And so, Solomon the king and preacher, with his thousands of proverbs, songs and sayings (and wives), sums up the end of the matter. Remember thy Creator. Remember Him in your youth, while it is still light. Before the darkness of this life or the time to come, when it is too late and tribulations and tragedies bring grief and sorrow. Before you die, and it's too late.

Before the day of the Lord.

The sun and the moon and the stars darkening is always a sign of the end, and the 2nd coming of Christ.

**Matthew 24:29-32**
*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Joel 2:31**
*The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come.*

There is a time it is too late to fear the Lord, to get right with Him, to remember our Creator.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

The day of the Lord will see the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men bow, every knee shall bow and tongue confess. The rich men and rulers will beg the rocks and mountains to fall upon them. They shall have their fear come upon them. The music will cease. The streets full of mourning.

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

The grinders shall cease, for there are few...

**Matthew 24:41-42**
*Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left. Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.*

The day of our death or the day of the Lord, the end comes for all men.

*Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern*.

If our bodies are broken, our spine snapped, our skull cracked, our heart stops and we bleed out, if our body can no longer move...And ever the curse of Adam is upon us;

*Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.*

**Genesis 3:19**
*In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

...All things considered, this is the ultimate vanity. *Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.*

The preacher is wise. The wisest man in history, filled with the Spirit of God to know things and the time and treasure to consider all the ways of man under the Sun. He sought understanding and set in order many proverbs, and taught the people knowledge. Seeking truth. Instruction in uprightness. Righteousness.

*The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.*

teachings.title: Absent from the body, present with the Lord
teachings.summary: Believers who die before the resurrection go consciously to Heaven rather than soul sleep, as the damned are in torment now and the souls under the altar cry how long, for created beings remain within time.
teachings.text:
Just to expand upon this point and why I believe the Bible teaches a intermediate stage for those in Christ whose physical body passes away now, before the day of the Lord, before the first resurrection, that our souls go to Heaven, not sleep or instantly regain consciousness at the resurrection as if no time had passed.

Most will agree that the Damned await in hell until the white Throne judgment where by they are cast into the lake of Fire. That their torment is immediate and without cease.

The Bible also talks about The souls of the righteous in Christ crying out "how long?" to God, awaiting His wrath.

Both of these imply that to us, to our souls or to our bodies, flesh or spirit, that we still exist within time as the created. That everlasting and eternal have no meaning outside of time.

That it's only the Creator who exists outside of time, time being a creation itself.

teachings.title: In the resurrection they neither marry
teachings.summary: Jesus answers the Sadducees that resurrected saints are like the angels who cannot marry, angels are never called sons of God, and the saints will judge in the millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
Continuing Mark chapter 12, we find the Sadducees come to bat, the Pharisees having struck out. They represent the secular Judaism we see today. Reform Jews make up the vast majority of so-called religious Jews, who eschew the spiritual and teach that there is no Heaven or Hell, and no resurrection. They believe they are to become gods on this earth, and teach that by their works, "healing the world" or tikkun olam as they call it, they can make a paradise on Earth where Jews naturally are the leaders of a global kingdom.

It isn't very far removed from the Orthodox Jew/Pharisaical religion of works-based righteousness and their inheritance of an earthly kingdom in the "time to come," just a bit more honest about their worship of self over God.

They seek to trip up Jesus with a very natural man Reddit-tier question regarding the law and the resurrection, thinking the one exposes a flaw in the other, and so bringing the entire thing down.

Jesus shows their sophistry easily. Angels cannot marry, or have relations the way humans do. In the resurrection, our glorified bodies will be like theirs.
(This is an unpopular take in our circles, but I am unmoved in my understanding that the Bible says at no time has God called the angels His sons, they cannot breed, and throughout scripture sons of God always refers to those saved by faith, who called upon His name for salvation, from the time of Seth onward)

Jesus again, being the word made flesh, having perfect understanding of all things as the creator of all things, could not be tested of natural man who cannot receive the things of God as they are spiritually discerned.

We are called to be as knowledgeable in these spiritual matters by understanding of scripture, that when the Kingdom comes, and the millennial reign over Earth takes place, we will serve as judges, stewards over those born in those days. And the least shall be first. The meek shall inherit the kingdom. Those who increased the master's yield by 100 fold will be given much, and those that buried what they were given will rule over nothing. Amen.

So study to show yourself approved unto God that you may be fruitful now, and a good and faithful servant in the Kingdom.

teachings.title: Thou that judgest doest the same things
teachings.theme: No respect of persons with God
teachings.summary: All, Jew or Gentile, are judged by the same law, so saved Christians must not judge hypocritically but be patient with new believers, knowing only grace spares them.
teachings.text:
Carrying over from Chapter 1, **Romans 2** sees Paul transition from the establishment of God's gospel, His revelation through His righteousness to them that believe, and His revelation via His wrath, especially to the reprobate, those given up by God.

He begins by reminding the reader that while the Reprobate is filled with unrighteousness, given over to a laundry list of sins, some unnatural, that there are many common to man. And if we judge them in their sin against the law, we need to remember we are judged by the same law with the same end, absent Christ.

That *the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such a things*.

If we judge by the law, we are convicted by the same law. But through His revelation, and in God's longsuffering forbearance and the goodness of God, His wrath and our guilt in the law should bring us to repentance, towards the Gospel of God.

Reprobate or unsaved, we store up wrath against ourselves and the righteous judgement of God, *who will render to every man according to his deeds.*

To them that are saved, who in patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honor and immortality, we are rendered eternal life.

But to them that are contentious, who dispute the judgment of God, and do not obey the truth by believing the Gospel, but obey unrighteousness, they are rendered God's indignation. His wrath.

There is no respect of persons with God.

He doesn't play favorites. Jew or Gentile. The judgment of God is the same. And we have no excuse.

Jews with the law, having the advantage of the oracles of God to show them His judgment, all are judged by the law, and Greek, the Gentiles, without the law are still aware as they accuse others or excuse others, because they have the law in their hearts and are given a conscience. Again, so man has no excuse.

Men think highly of themselves by judging themselves against others in the law. Jew or Greek. Men deny the judgment of God by excusing those who do as they do, Jew or Greek.

Hypocrisy and cope.

But all come to the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to the Gospel.

All have sinned. The wages of sin are death. But in Christ we are forgiven. Paul will flesh this out more, but here is the beginning of the Romans' Road. The broad outline of the Gospel presentation that has led millions to Christ using the doctrines found in the book of Romans; all face judgment by the same law of God and the Gospel of Christ.

Jews, with their book-knowledge of the law, who see themselves as understanding His judgments, work to be instructors to the unregenerate Gentile, a light to guide (which they ought to be, by God's design), Paul asks, are they keeping the law they have confidence in? Are they hypocrites?

At the time of this writing, believing Jews made up most of the churches, and they were gifted to give the understanding of the scriptures to the new believers coming from a pagan background, unlearned to the prophets of God. Paul asks, do you practice what you preach, because by their hypocrisy the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles.

Saved Christians, especially those who have been in the faith for any length of time, or who were raised by Bible believing parents in a Bible teaching church, are in a like manner in the position of the Jews.

And in a like manner, many judge the unregenerate and unlearned by the law, while they themselves are guilty of the same, and there but for the grace of God deserve the same fate.

We set ourselves as instructors of the word of God, to guide the babes in Christ, but do we sin as we judge against them in their sin? It applies to us now as much as to the 1st Century converted Jews.

We ought not think too highly of ourselves, remembering we deserve the same judgment as even the worst Reprobate; Death and Hell.

And as we teach new Christians, we should be as patient and longsuffering as God is towards us. Having the grace to understand we all sin and fall short.

teachings.title: Ambassadors of reconciliation
teachings.summary: Our letters of commendation are the souls we win, our glorified body is sure but clothed by our works, and as new men reconciled to God we are ambassadors bringing others the same reconciliation.
teachings.text:
Continuing the theme of the previous chapters, which of you recall, started regarding letters of commendation among men. Paul reminds that our letters of commendation are those who have believed because of our sharing the gospel. He says we are being judged by the conscience of the unbelieving, that our behavior should reflect the light that's within us, living as a light that guides them through the darkness put over them by the devil, winning them to Christ.  That we are ministers of the same Gospel of mercy that changed our hearts and brought us to focus on the things unseen, our conscience clear in Jesus.

Building on this, Paul writes about our physical bodies perishing, but our glorified body from Heaven assured. That the Holy Spirit within us is the earnest, the down payment from God on His promise. But our eternal body is naked, being new born. It is clothed and housed in raiment earned by our works here, judged by God, and so we should constantly strive in this body for that which we will receive in the next.

Preferring being absent this body to be present with the Lord, we should live without fear. What are we threatened with? Heaven? As Jesus said "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." We should live with the confidence that this is true and that we are furnishing the mansion He has provided us, winning souls to Christ.

By focusing on the unseen, living the faith, we also give answer to those that judge by appearance rather than of the heart, as God judges. And in doing so, be able to pierce the veil of darkness and bring them to the light of God reflected in us.

We are a new man, contained in the earthen vessels of the old, but reconciled with God in Jesus, and so, given the ministry, being a servant, to spreading that reconciliation to others. Ambassadors.

Paul says it better than I can, go read the first 5 chapters again.

teachings.title: Hell is real, and Mary had other children
teachings.summary: Jesus preached Hell often, and Matthew 13 names Jesus' brothers and sisters, refuting Mary's perpetual virginity.
teachings.text:
And when Jesus says that the tares should be burned in the fire, the wailing and gnashing of teeth, he is preaching on Hell. Those falsely claiming there is no Hell, or that Christ didn't talk about it are lying. He does frequently, yet many whose heart is by the wayside, or even the stoney ground, blindly believe the lies, having no root in the truth of the word.

As for the Mary worshipers, another L.

*Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?* *And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?*

His half-brothers and sisters, Mary not a perpetual virgin. Sick and twisted false doctrine rebuked, amen.

teachings.title: Abel's blood sacrifice and Cain's works
teachings.summary: Abel was accepted by faith in the blood sacrifice while Cain was rejected for offering his own works, and the shedding of innocent blood cries out from the earth and brings judgment on a land.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:4**
*By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.*

Now fallen, cast out from Eden, Adam and Eve, the mother of man are fruitful and multiply.

And her first born, a man from God is Cain, a tiller of the earth. Working the fields.

We know from Genesis 3 the burden God placed on fallen man.

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

Cain, under this burden grew herbs and vegetables, fruit of the land. With sweat of his brow. *Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the* Lord*.*

And God respected not his sacrifice.

And Abel, a keeper of sheep, *he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the* Lord *had respect unto Abel and to his offering.*

The firstling lamb. The sacrifice of blood for attornment. The Bible says Abel *by faith* brought the sacrifice that was acceptable unto the Lord.

But Cain brought his works and was rejected.

But God, long suffering and who the Bible says would not that any man perish, gives His word to Cain, to repent towards the faith, in the blood of the lamb for remission of sin, as He had given Adam and Eve, that Abel gained God's pleasure by.

*And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.*

Unable to get past his own pride and accept God's promise, His word, Cain allowed his wrath in, and in covetousness slew innocent Abel, and the very earth cries out to the Lord that his blood had been spilled.

This is a Biblical doctrine that's often overlooked. The spilling of innocent blood actually causes the earth itself to cry out to God. We see several times throughout scripture God warns man against it;

*That innocent blood be not shed in thy land, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.*
**Deuteronomy 19:10**

*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now*.
**Romans 8:22**

*The blood of their sons and their daughters,*
*Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan;*
*And the land was polluted with the blood.*
**Psalm 106:38**

One of the things that curses a land and brings judgement on a people is innocent blood shed. It pollutes the land, and the earth travails and groans, crying out to the Lord.

And so undone, Cain is cursed.

When we reject God's word, His gift of salvation in the blood of Christ, the lamb slain at the foundation of the world,  when we count on our works and want credit from God for our own righteousness, we invite sin into our heart, and when we reject God's word finally, are rejected of Him. Marked as Cain.

teachings.title: Blotted Out, Never Added to the Book of Life
teachings.summary: All are born into the book of life and are only blotted out through unbelief, reprobation or unpardonable sin; no one is ever added to it.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars;*

Again, Jesus is addressing a church, this in Sardis, and He uses descriptors of Himself from scripture to sign the message.
