 *I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.*
*Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.*

The church at Sardis has a reputation for being an active and lively congregation, but Jesus says He knows that's not the case. He warns them to return to what was preached unto them, that they won't die out completely. That His coming won't be a surprise to them, like a thief in the night overtaking them as He will the world of non-believers.

*Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy.*

His appeal then are to the genuinely saved among them in Sardis, encouraging them in their walk, and their reward in His return.

And then, again another message to the saved, who have overcome the world by their faith in Him:

*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

The white raiment of the wedding feast, the garment we receive having been called by grace and accepting the invitation by faith. Whose names are not blotted out of the book of life.

Note, we are born into the book of life, we are blotted out by death as unbelievers, or reprobation, or unpardonable sin such as blasphemy of the Holy Ghost, knowingly adding to or taking away from the word of God or, as we will see, taking the mark of the beast. No one in the Bible is added to the book of life, only blotted out and removed having already been there. Understanding of this helps when faced with a few false doctrines.

Jesus promise to us who are saved is that He will confess our names before our Father, our counsel, the sole mediator we need.

teachings.title: The battle of Armageddon
teachings.summary: At Armageddon Christ defeats the beast's armies with the sword of His mouth, casting the antichrist and false prophet into the lake of fire and leaving the wicked to the fowls.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 13:9**
*Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.*

**Joel 3:12-14**
*Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.*

*Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.*

Armageddon, the "Mountain of Assembly," refers to Mt Zion. The valley of Jehoshaphat, the valley of judgment, is the space between Zion and Mt Olive, where Christ will rule during the Millennial Reign.

It is here the armies of the beast assemble and ride out to battle Jesus,
King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords.

*And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.*

The antichrist and his false prophet are instantly cast into the lake of fire. The remnant of their armies slain by the sword that comes from the mouth of Christ. The two-edged sword, which immediately calls to mind the word of God. Spoken from Jesus mouth, with the power to slay the wicked, leaving their carcasses for the carrion birds to feed on.

**Jeremiah 7:33**
*And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.*

**Ezekiel 39:17**
*And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood.*

teachings.title: The Harrowing of Hell is a Catholic fable
teachings.summary: The Catholic Harrowing of Hell misuses 1 Peter 4:6, which in context means the dead in Hell were shown their disobedience by Christ's resurrection, as those mocking Noah were destroyed in the flood.
teachings.text:
There is a false doctrine, invented by Catholics (among dozens of others), called the "Harrowing of Hell." In it, they say that Jesus didn't go to Hell for 3 days and 3 nights to be the burnt sin offering (a holocaust), for the whole world as the sole propitiation for our sins, as the Bible teaches. Instead they claim Jesus went to Hell on a Saturday to give the Gospel to Old Testament saints and various heathens who "lived a righteous life," or were "seekers of truth" like Virgil and Plato and other pagans, so they could go with Him to Heaven.

It is an incredibly natural man thing to believe, and it's no wonder that its origin comes from the false "Gospel of Nicodemus," supposedly written by the unsaved Pharisee in the Gospel of John who couldn't understand salvation and being born again, despite being a leader of the people, as Jesus pointed out.

*Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?*

But to give it some anchor in scripture, they pull **1 Peter 4:6** to claim it. The verse states "*For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead..."* Which relates back to the previous chapter:

**1 Peter 3**
*8 Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:*

*9 Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.*

*10 For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:*

*11 Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.*

*12 For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.*

*13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?*

*14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;*

*15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

*16 Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

*17 For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.*

*18 For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:*

*19 By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;*

*20 Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.*

*21 The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:*

*22 Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.*

Jesus triumph over death and Hell and the eternal destruction of those in prison, Hell, is a like image to the people destroyed in the flood, the dead in sin, and the quick are those with eternal life in Christ, by the resurrection of Jesus, like Noah and the other 7, saved by water, (which is also a figure of baptism, which is *an answer of a good conscience toward God,* not how we are saved, but that we are saved).

The people in Hell were shown their disobedience by the resurrection of Jesus, just as they mocked Noah and were destroyed by the flood, they mocked God and were thrown into Hell to witness Jesus triumph.

teachings.title: The burden of Babylon and the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: Isaiah's prophecy against Babylon has a dual fulfillment, in the fall of the Babylonian empire and in the destruction of the spirit of Babylon in the wrath to come, when no silver or gold can deliver.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Isaiah against Babylon, they the day of the Lord is at hand, clearly has dual fulfillment. It speaks not only of the destruction of Babylonian empire, which had only risen to prominence in the days of Isaiah, but that same spirit of Babylon which will be destroyed in the wrath to come.

...*cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine. And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.*

**Malachi 3:2**
*But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?*

And as Isaiah preached, the Persians and Medes had no regard for gold and silver, the Lord's judgment can't be swayed either.

**Zephaniah 1:18**
*Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.*

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

teachings.title: The heavens declare the glory of God
teachings.summary: Creation and conscience reveal God's power and law to all men so that they are without excuse, while His written word gives the hope of mercy and leads to salvation.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 19** is fairly short, yet packed with doctrine, teaching the purpose of creation, the testimony of God to all creatures, the picture of Christ, and the establishment of the law of the Lord in nature itself, that there is no excuse, while the believer is given constant reminders of His judgements.

**Romans 1:18–20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse*

The heavens declare the glory of God. Looking upon the night sky we see His precision and power. And as the day follows day and night follows night, each with the passing of the sun and the stars, we are given evidence of His might.

The things of creation speak without words, that all man may understand. They don't need a language. They don't need to be explained. Man sees the passage of time, seasons, years, decades even, in heavenly bodies.

The vain hypothetical of a savage on a remote island, never hearing the gospel, is undone by the understanding that all nature is a parable and a testament of God, showing men truth.

The boldness of the sun breaking forth in the morning is as the risen Christ, returning in glory, a picture of the Creator Who is blessed forever, amen.

Nature teaches us God's law. His ways.

**1 Corinthians 11:14**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?*

His wrath is revealed against those who sin, even without the oracles of God documenting His commandments. The Spirit showing mankind the results of their transgressions. The understanding that murder, adultery, lying, stealing, all of these things that do harm to your neighbor and are a shame before God, are known.

**Romans 2:11–16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified. For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

Man can see the law of God, know it written in their hearts, watch the outcome of their behavior and the wrath upon those who sin, and know they are guilty before the consuming fire which is God.

How much more are we who have His statutes and commandments by the oracles of God?

**Romans 3:1–2**
*What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.*

The advantage given Israel, and held by the Jews in Paul's day, is now given to the world. That everyone may know His word.

*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.*

If the day declares His righteousness and the night His knowledge, and the very nature of things speaks to His wrath, then the oracles of God give us the hope of His mercy. God is a rewarder to those that diligently seek Him.

The fear of the Lord is clean, and known to all men. The fool may say in their heart there is no God, but the wise fear Him, even if they don't know scripture.

The truth is more desirable than gold, sweeter than honey. Its pursuit is its own reward, spurring us to seek Him. The warnings and rewards, motivation to learn His ways.

And, in that knowledge, we find His word, and from that word, salvation.
